learningObjectives: Identify the major components of the Corpus Callosum.
Explain how the Corpus Callosum contributes to distributed brain function.
Connect Corpus Callosum physiology with clinically relevant symptoms and conditions.
Interpret structural or functional findings cautiously and in context.

anatomy.label: Rostrum
anatomy.clinical: Supports integration of affective and decision signals.

anatomy.label: Genu
anatomy.clinical: Relevant to executive and social-cognitive integration.

anatomy.label: Body
anatomy.detail: Carries fibres between frontal, parietal and motor regions.

anatomy.label: Isthmus
anatomy.detail: Links parietal and temporal association areas.

anatomy.label: Splenium
anatomy.detail: Connects occipital and posterior temporal cortices.
anatomy.clinical: Damage can produce alexia without agraphia in specific lesion patterns.

quizBank.question: Which component is best described as: Posterior association connector?
